passages.title: Seema and repetitive acts
passages.text: Reeva noticed that Seema washes her hands very frequently. In addition to this, she used to walk only within the patterns drawn on the floor or road. Further, it was noticed that she was unable to control her preoccupation with specific ideas and failed to prevent herself from repeatedly carrying out a particular act or a series of acts. Therefore, Seema experiences anxiety and disturbances in her life. These pattern of thoughts and behaviour have affected her ability to carry out normal activities.

passages.title: Abby and behavioural therapy
passages.text: Abby is very annoying by nature. He does not follow what his parents say and refuses to obey them. He constantly bothers his parents and classmates with his improper behavior and does not regularly complete the homework given by his teachers. After seeing Abby's behavior, his parents take him to a psychotherapist in order to understand why he behaves the way he does. The psychotherapist planned to administer behavioural therapy for modifying his behaviour.

questions.stem: What level of stress is suitable for optimal performance?

match.front: How do too much stress and too little stress each affect performance?
match.back: High stress too can produce unpleasant effects and cause our performance to deteriorate. Conversely, too little stress may cause one to feel somewhat listless and low on motivation which may lead us to perform slowly and less efficiently.

questions.stem: During stressful situations, the adrenal gland releases large amounts of ________ into the blood stream.

match.front: Physiological stress response: the two pathways started by the hypothalamus.
match.back:
The first pathway involves the autonomic nervous system. The adrenal gland releases large amount of catecholamines (epinephrine and norepinephrine) into the blood stream. This leads to physiological changes seen in fight-or-flight response.
The second pathway involves the pituitary gland, which secretes the corticosteroid (cortisol) which provides energy.

questions.stem: In which stage of Selye's General Adaptation Syndrome, the presence of noxious stimulus or stressor leads to the activation of the adrenal-pituitary-cortex system?

match.front: GAS stage 1: what happens in the alarm reaction stage?
match.back: The presence of a noxious stimulus or stressor leads to activation of the adrenal-pituitary-cortex system. This triggers the release of hormones producing the stress response. Now the individual is ready for fight or flight.

questions.stem: International Classification of Diseases (ICD-10) was prepared by:

match.back: The classification scheme officially used in India and elsewhere is the tenth revision of the International Classification of Diseases (ICD-10), which is known as the ICD-10 Classification of Behavioural and Mental Disorders. It was prepared by the World Health Organisation (WHO).

questions.stem: Low activity of gamma aminobutyric acid (GABA) neurotransmitter has been linked to:

match.back:

Anxiety disorders have been linked to low activity of the neurotransmitter gamma aminobutyric acid (GABA), schizophrenia to excess activity of dopamine, and depression to low activity of serotonin.

Compulsive behaviour is the need to perform certain behaviours over and over again.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not a technique used in behaviour therapy?

match.front: Aaron Beck's cognitive therapy: the aim is to achieve what, which in turn reduces anxiety and depression?
match.back: The questions make the client think in a direction opposite to that of the negative automatic thoughts whereby s/he gains insight into the nature of her/his dysfunctional schemas, and is able to alter her/his cognitive structures. The aim of the therapy is to achieve this cognitive restructuring which, in turn, reduces anxiety and depression.

questions.stem: In which of the following disorders, aversive conditioning is most suitable technique for treatment?

match.front: An alcoholic is given a mild electric shock and asked to smell the alcohol. Which technique is this?
match.back:
Aversive conditioning
For example, an alcoholic is given a mild electric shock and asked to smell the alcohol. With repeated pairings the smell of alcohol is aversive as the pain of the shock is associated with it and the person will give up alcohol.
